title: Chaos test scheduler for quarterly controlled regional failovers (repeatable + auto-reporting)
creator: Miles Thornton
description:
Background
- We completed the first controlled failover game day (us-east → eu-west) and learned that the hardest part to repeat is not the routing flip itself, but consistently running the same pre-flight checks, applying blast-radius constraints, capturing timeline annotations, and producing a shareable report.
- We also want a predictable cadence (quarterly) so multi-region readiness doesn’t drift.

Goal
Build a lightweight “chaos test scheduler” that makes controlled regional failovers repeatable, safe-by-default, and automatically reported.

Scope
In-scope
- Scheduling and orchestration for controlled failover runs (staging + production).
- Guardrails to limit blast radius (tenant allowlist, route/model allowlist, max % traffic, max flips per hour).
- Automated pre-flight checks (signals healthy, capacity headroom, probes green, dashboards/alerts loaded).
- Automated timeline/report generation (metrics snapshots + decision/audit trail links).
- Integrations:
  - Failover controller dry-run + execute endpoints
  - Region health service + perf-canary reachability probes
  - Audit events / timeline annotations
  - Incident-bot notifications (start/stop/abort + summary)

Out of scope
- General-purpose chaos framework for all services.
- Fully automated no-human-in-the-loop production execution for all tiers (we will still require explicit approvals until we meet exit criteria).

Proposed design (high-level)
- A small “failover-runner” service/job (K8s CronJob in staging; scheduled job + manual trigger in prod) that:
  1) Resolves a test plan/scenario (e.g., us-east → eu-west, Hosted only, 5% traffic).
  2) Runs pre-flight checks and produces a Go/No-Go bundle.
  3) Executes controller in dry-run mode; posts recommended actions + evidence signals.
  4) If approved, triggers the controlled failover (controller execute) and watches abort conditions.
  5) Collects metrics/time series snapshots and audit events; emits annotations.
  6) Posts a report summary and links to a stored artifact (Confluence page or Drive doc).

Guardrails / Safety requirements
- Default must be “dry-run only” unless explicitly enabled via feature flag + approval hook.
- Strict blast-radius limits (configurable per environment):
  - tenant allowlist required in prod
  - max traffic percentage cap (default 1% prod)
  - max duration (e.g., 15 min) with automatic rollback
  - abort conditions (e.g., 5xx burn > threshold for N minutes, tail latency burn > threshold, control plane errors)
- Rate limiting: scheduler must respect controller anti-flap and per-tenant flip limits.
- Clear ownership and escalation: if abort triggers, page on-call and roll back immediately.

Reporting requirements
- Auto-generated report should include:
  - scenario + config (regions, routes/models, tenant set, traffic cap, approval identities)
  - start/end timestamps + key milestones (dry-run computed, execute started, traffic moved, stabilized, rollback)
  - failover time (detection→decision, decision→traffic shifted), error/latency impact, capacity headroom before/after
  - audit event links + dashboard links
  - issues found + follow-ups (auto-created checklist section)

Success criteria / Acceptance criteria
- Scheduler can run a controlled failover in staging on a weekly cadence with no manual steps beyond approval.
- Scheduler can be invoked in production with tenant allowlist + traffic cap and produces a complete report.
- The run creates consistent annotations on the failover dashboards and incident timeline.
- Abort conditions reliably stop the run and trigger rollback + notification.

Links / References
- Game day plan: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/game-days/controlled-failover-test-plan-q1-2026.json
- Game day results: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/game-days/controlled-failover-test-results-2026-01-15.json
- Runbook: sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/routing-policy-failover-controller-runbook.json
- Dashboard spec: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/failover-signal-dashboards-spec.json
- Controller dry-run: sources/github/redwood/pr-19814-failover-controller-dry-run.json
- Simulation endpoint (for rehearsal): sources/github/redwood/pr-19828-add-failover-simulate-endpoint.json
- Incident-bot summaries: sources/github/incident-bot/pr-412-add-failover-event-summaries.json

Open questions
- Where should the “source of truth” for scheduled scenarios live (repo config vs Console vs Confluence)?
- Do we want separate cadences for Hosted vs Dedicated, or one combined run with multiple phases?
- What’s the minimal approval flow for production (single on-call ack vs dual-approval)?

Implementation checklist
- [ ] Define scenario config schema (regions, tier, routes/models, tenant allowlist, traffic cap, max duration, abort thresholds)
- [ ] Implement pre-flight checks module (reachability probes, region health freshness, capacity headroom, controller readiness)
- [ ] Integrate with controller dry-run + execute + rollback endpoints
- [ ] Add “reporter” that generates a structured summary + persists artifact
- [ ] Add dashboard annotations + incident timeline hooks
- [ ] Add incident-bot messages for scheduled runs (start, approval requested, success, aborted)
- [ ] Staging weekly schedule + production manual-trigger with guardrails
- [ ] Update runbooks + on-call training note for quarterly cadence
comments: 2026-01-20 (Miles Thornton): Follow-up from Game Day #1 retro — we need repeatable execution and a consistent report artifact, otherwise each run is a bespoke effort and we keep re-learning the same steps. Creating this ticket to formalize the scheduler + auto-reporting workstream.

2026-01-23 (Allison Grant): Reporting should include the exact dashboard URLs + query params and must add automation-driven annotations; during the test we lacked clear markers and the timeline was hard to reconstruct. Please include an explicit “annotation emitter” in the runner.

2026-01-27 (Devon Price): Incident-bot can post a thread per scheduled run (like an incident-lite) with a pinned summary and links. We’ll need a stable run_id to correlate messages, audit events, and annotations.

2026-02-03 (Benji Okafor): I’ll take this. Proposal: runner as a small service with scenario configs in-repo (versioned) + feature flag gating. Pre-flight checks will hard-fail if allowlist missing in prod. Will sync with Rafael/Miles on abort thresholds to align with burn alerts (ENG-2418).

2026-02-14 (Rafael Mendes): Please ensure the scheduler supports Dedicated drain sequencing later (ENG-2420) even if MVP is Hosted-only. At minimum, keep the scenario schema extensible so we can add a ‘drain_required=true’ phase.
